title: Surgical protocol for precise and high-throughput viral injections in rhesus monkey brain
author: Tangen, Harmon, et al.

steps.title: Make sagittal skin incision
steps.instruction: Using a #10 surgical blade, cut a single midline sagittal incision along the pre‑marked line, keeping the blade in continuous motion without lifting, and apply gentle thumb‑index pressure to keep the wound slightly open; preserve the galea and control any bleeding with sterile gauze.

steps.title: Open galea layer
steps.instruction: Insert the sharp end of a periosteal elevator into the midline to cut through the galea for a few millimetres, then separate the galea from the skull with the elevator and cut it using Mayo scissors opened only a few millimetres and slid forward to produce a smooth continuous incision (alternatively a #15 blade may be used).

steps.title: Retract galea
steps.instruction: Separate the galea from the deep temporalis fascia with a periosteal elevator or closed‑blade Mayo scissors, apply gentle traction, and optionally use dry gauze to push the galea laterally.

steps.title: Retract temporalis muscles
steps.instruction: Detach the dorsal temporalis tendons from the skull using the sharp edge of a periosteal elevator oriented sagittally, then gradually elevate the tendons; subsequently detach the bulk of the temporalis muscles with muscle curettes (or controlled horizontal movements of the elevator).

steps.title: Perform craniotomy and bone flap removal
steps.instruction: Create a craniotomy extending ~10 mm beyond planned injection sites (measure AP boundaries from ear‑bar level and ML boundaries from midline); drill with an ultrasonic piezoelectric cutter or circular wheel, leaving a thin bone layer over the dura and especially over the sagittal sinus (use a bore drill bit centrally if needed); lift the bone flap starting caudally with two periosteal elevators, gently separate adhesions, avoid inverting the opposite edge, and store the flap in a sterile bowl of saline. Irrigate the exposed dura, apply a small piece of neurosurgical patty (or gel‑foam for major bleeding) for hemostasis, then remove it before closure. Create four suture holes ~3 mm from the craniotomy edge (angle drill slightly), shielding the dura with a brain spatula while drilling; smooth sharp edges with rongeurs and apply bone wax to bleeding bone, removing excess wax before dura opening.

steps.title: Measure sagittal sinus coordinates
steps.instruction: Mount the injection micromanipulator on the stereotaxic frame (cut disposable drapes if present), avoid bending the injection needle, place the manipulator at the most caudal AP target (coarse AP set, fine dial zero), then adjust ML and DV until the needle tip gently contacts the middle of the sagittal sinus; record ML and DV values, repeat for each AP target, and have a second person cross‑check all coordinates.

steps.title: Open dura mater
steps.instruction: Using a #11 blade on a #7 handle, make a small nick in the dura with the blade back parallel to the cortex; lift the nicked edge with fine forceps, then cut through the dura with the blade or iris scissors kept 1–2 mm open, gliding forward rather than closing; continue the incision until cerebrospinal fluid appears, taking extra care at rostral and caudal ends to avoid the sagittal sinus. Maintain at least a 5 mm margin from the craniotomy edge.

steps.title: Prime injection circuit and deliver virus
steps.instruction: Verify flow through the injection circuit; start at a high rate (~20 µL min⁻¹) to fill dead volume, then reduce to 1–5 µL min⁻¹ until viral efflux is seen at the needle tip, then stop or lower to ~0.01 µL min⁻¹. Adjust AP/ML to the target, lower the needle just above cortex, inspect for surface vessels and shift if needed (skip site if no vessel‑free entry). Penetrate cortex, advance to target depth (maintaining a minimal flow ~0.01 µL min⁻¹ during descent if desired), set the injection pump to the planned rate, and irrigate dura/cortex with sterile saline every 2–3 min.

steps.title: Irrigate cortex and wait post‑injection
steps.instruction: Continue saline irrigation of the exposed cortex every 2–3 min during injection; after the programmed volume is delivered, wait 10 min before needle withdrawal to reduce backflow.

steps.title: Withdraw needle slowly
steps.instruction: Retract the needle very slowly over the first 2–3 mm to avoid negative pressure; confirm viral flow at the end of each injection once the needle is out. For multiple injections along one track, proceed from the most ventral to the most superficial site and reduce the inter‑injection wait to 1 min.

steps.title: Flush cortical surface before closure
steps.instruction: Remove the micromanipulators from the stereotaxic arms and flush the cortical surface with normal saline, ensuring no blood clots or bleeding remain.

steps.title: Suture dura mater
steps.instruction: Using fine forceps and a Castroviejo needle holder, place a continuous suture of 5‑0 or 6‑0 monofilament (absorbable or non‑absorbable) on a tapered needle, spacing stitches 1–1.5 mm apart and taking bites <1 mm from the margin; if severe swelling occurs, leave the dura open and cover with an artificial graft.

steps.title: Replace bone flap with sutures
steps.instruction: Thread 3‑0 or 2‑0 multifilament absorbable suture tails through the pre‑drilled holes (~3 mm from the craniotomy edge), pull them through the corresponding holes on the bone flap, tie each with a square knot (two opposite single knots), gradually tighten alternating sides to avoid uneven tension, avoid over‑pulling, and finish with one or two additional single knots to secure the flap.

steps.title: Close fascia (galea)
steps.instruction: Close the galea using a continuous 3‑0 multifilament absorbable suture placed 3–4 mm apart, ensuring both rostral and caudal ends are securely approximated.

steps.title: Close skin incision
steps.instruction: Close the skin with a 3‑0 monofilament absorbable suture in an intradermal pattern (or alternatively a 3‑0/2‑0 non‑absorbable suture in a horizontal mattress placed ~2 mm from the margin and 4 mm apart); note that non‑absorbable sutures are removed after 10–14 days.

steps.title: Post‑operative recovery monitoring
steps.instruction: After extubation, place the animal in an ICU with heat and supplemental O₂, monitor continuously until consciousness returns; provide oral rehydration drink, then next day offer moistened chow, fruit, water and rehydration drink. Monitor at least twice daily for mentation, mobility, seizures, and other neurological signs; keep the animal in ICU for a minimum of 3 days because brain swelling may peak at 48–72 h.

steps.title: Open skull for terminal extraction
steps.instruction: Under anesthesia, repeat the earlier draping and skin/galea opening steps, taking special care with adhesions from the previous surgery; detach temporalis muscles to the occipital ridge, detach trapezius to expose its ventral aspect, drill the skull following the pattern shown in Figure 16 (thick lines for injection craniotomy, thin lines for terminal extraction), then lift bone flaps with periosteal elevators without fully removing them, proceeding cautiously because the original flap may be adherent to dura.

steps.title: Transcardial perfusion with cold ssACSF
steps.instruction: Place the animal supine on saline‑soaked gauze, make a midline incision from clavicles to pelvis with a #22 blade, perform thoracotomy, open diaphragm and pericardium to expose the heart, clamp the descending aorta, cut the right auricle to open the right atrium, excise the heart apex, insert a large‑bore olive‑tip cannula through the apex into the left ventricle and advance into the ascending aorta, clamp the apex, then connect a peristaltic pump set to 100 mL min⁻¹ delivering 1.5–2 L of ice‑cold, fully oxygenated, continuously bubbled ssACSF; perfuse until vessels are clear (≈10–20 min).

steps.title: Extract brain rapidly
steps.instruction: Turn the animal prone, remove the drilled bone flaps with rongeurs, dissect posterior dura over occipital lobes and along the midsagittal plane to remove falx cerebri and tentorium, transect the cervical spinal cord, bluntly dissect cranial nerves with the flat end of a scalpel handle, and lift the brain out of the skull in a caudal‑to‑rostral direction, minimizing any remaining attachments.

steps.title: Block brain into coronal slabs
steps.instruction: Immediately place the brain in a brain mold and continuously irrigate with cold oxygenated ssACSF; using the mold, cut full coronal slabs following the guide (start with the most rostral cut, e.g., temporal pole), hemisect the brain, further block individual structures as needed, and transfer each block into sealed containers with cold oxygenated ssACSF (storage 15–30 min preserves tissue for electrophysiology).

steps.title: Slice tissue blocks into thin sections
steps.instruction: Trim each block to ~1–1.5 cm, adhere it to a specimen stage with cyanoacrylate, then section 250–400 µm slices on a vibratome (e.g., Leica VT‑1200S) while submerged in ice‑cold oxygenated ssACSF.

steps.title: Incubate slices and store
steps.instruction: Transfer slices to a submerged incubation chamber containing oxygenated ssACSF warmed to 32–34 °C, incubate for 30 min at that temperature, then keep slices under sterile conditions at 32–34 °C; inspect the solution daily for contamination or evaporation and replace as needed. Slices remain viable for 3–5 days (solution exchange optional after 15–30 min if sterility is maintained).

steps.title: Prepare slices for electrophysiology
steps.instruction: Allow slices to recover for at least 1 h after slicing, then move individual slices to the recording setup for ex vivo electrophysiological experiments.

description: Stereotaxic surgery is a common technique in systems neuroscience for performing precise microinjection in the nonhuman primate brain.2,3 Despite the wide use of stereotaxic procedures, detailed methods are rarely included in published studies. This protocol provides a step-by-step guide for performing high-precision stereotaxic viral injections in macaques. The procedures described here were developed and optimized for the experiments reported in previous publications.1,4,5,6,7,8 Using this approach, a wide range of viral vectors and payloads (e.g., GFP, RFP, ChR2) have been effectively delivered, including adeno-associated viruses (AAVs), particularly AAV-PHP.eB, an engineered AAV9 capsid variant, and lentiviral vectors. Although the core surgical framework is broadly applicable across viral vector types, injection parameters (e.g., volume, rate, and post-injection survival time) may require optimization depending on vector characteristics and experimental goals. In addition to viral injection, the same general framework can be adapted for other stereotaxic and surgical applications in nonhuman primates, including tracer injections, excitotoxic lesion studies, and chronic cranial implantations. Beyond the injection procedure, this protocol describes how to extract the brain for ex vivo electrophysiological studies, which differs from commonly used post-euthanasia extraction used for anatomical or histological analyses. We also introduce a custom-designed injection circuit that enables simultaneous multiple injections, improving reliability and substantially reducing surgical duration. In developing this protocol, we incorporated and expanded upon established methods in the literature, such as the use of tooth markers,9 and sagittal sinus alignment.10 Finally, we further optimized the previously published surgical protocols11,12,13 and injection-circuit designs.14 All procedures were conducted in accordance with the guidelines approved by the National Institute of
